And the sign of this: She sat under the date-palm (Judges 4:5), and our Sages said (Megillah 14): Just as the date-palm has only one heart, so too Israel.' (2) Even if the analogy were treated as implicit bechina, only two conceptual poles are present (the date-palm/unity on one side, Israel/unity of heart on the other) — this is a single pair, not a 3-node cluster. A package requires at minimum a connected component that illuminates a distinct thematic domain with multiple expressions. A two-term analogy does not meet this threshold. CONCLUSION: No packages can be proposed for Torah #269. This Torah should be flagged as a candidate for future data enrichment if scholars identify extended bechina structure in related commentaries or expanded versions of the teaching.
